_note: The customer is on X12 passthrough, so the snippet is raw X12 and the fix lives in their EDI translator, not in a JSON map. BSN05 is the Hierarchical Structure Code; 0001 is Shipment/Order/Packaging/Item, 0004 is Shipment/Order/Item. The guideline requirement is invented.

errors.message: Element BSN05 (Hierarchical Structure Code) value "0001" is not allowed by RETAILER01 856 guideline. Allowed: "0004" (Shipment, Order, Item)

customer_note: Our 856s to Retailer One are Invalid but the same ASN format works fine for our three other retailers.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Retailer One's 856 guideline requires structure 0004 (Shipment, Order, Item) in BSN05 and the customer's translator emits 0001 for every partner; on X12 passthrough the fix is in their translator's partner profile, not in a map on our side
hypotheses.check: Confirm the tier from the raw ISA in the snippet, then check the guideline PDF for BSN05 allowed codes

hypotheses.hypothesis: A rule could rewrite BSN05, but the HL loop must also match 0004, so a code-only fix would validate the header and ship a wrong body
hypotheses.check: Look at the HL hierarchy in the failing ASN for a P (pack) level

mock_result.customer_reply: Retailer One requires a different ASN structure from your other retailers: Shipment, Order, Item without a pack level, which is code 0004 in BSN05. Your ASN uses code 0001 with a packaging level. Since you send raw X12, this is a partner-specific setting in your EDI translator. Once the Retailer One profile emits the 0004 structure, the ASNs will validate. Their guideline is linked for reference.

ticket_two.title: 856 hierarchical structure codes by partner (0001 vs 0004)
ticket_two.why: Every passthrough customer that adds this retailer hits the same requirement. A short article with the BSN05 code, the HL layout, and a sample ASN removes a ticket per onboarding.
